module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sum of two squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5

Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ where $a, b, c, d$ are
nonnegative integers.

Zhi-Wei Sun has offered a \$3,500 prize for the first proof.

*References:*
- [A303656](https://oeis.org/A303656)
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of four squares," arXiv preprint:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05868v10
- Z.-W. Sun, "Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem," Journal of Number Theory:
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of three or four squares":
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/Square-sum.pdf
- Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations:
  https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA303656

/-- The predicate that `n` can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ for nonnegative integers. -/
def A (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d : ℕ, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + 3 ^ c + 5 ^ d

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : A 2 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : A 3 :=
  ⟨1, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : A 4 :=
  ⟨1, 1, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : A 5 :=
  ⟨0, 1, 1, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : A 6 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 1, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_25 : A 25 :=
  ⟨1, 4, 1, 1, by norm_num⟩

/--
**Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture (A303656)**: Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as the sum of two
squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : A n := by
  sorry

end OeisA303656

findings.description:
The module docstring's last reference reads "Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations: https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf". The title and the URL name two different papers, and neither is about the formalised conjecture.

- The URL resolves to F. Petrov and Z.-W. Sun, "Proof of some conjectures involving quadratic residues", Electronic Research Archive 28(2) (2020) 589-597, doi:10.3934/era.2020031. That paper is about products and permutations involving quadratic residues mod p. It says nothing about sums of squares and powers.
- The quoted title belongs to A. Machiavelo and N. Tsopanidis, "Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 Conjecture and Variations", J. Number Theory 222 (2021) 1-20, arXiv:2003.02592. That paper is about a different conjecture: every n in N is x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2 with x+3y+5z a square. It never mentions a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d.

The pairing is also misleading about status. The 1-3-5 conjecture has been proved, while the a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d conjecture stated here is open. The Lean statements are not affected.
findings.source_evidence:
- The PDF at the cited URL begins: "ELECTRONIC RESEARCH ARCHIVE doi:10.3934/era.2020031 Volume 28, Number 2, June 2020 pp. 589-597 PROOF OF SOME CONJECTURES INVOLVING QUADRATIC RESIDUES Fedor Petrov ... Zhi-Wei Sun".
- arXiv:2003.02592 (abs page and LaTeX source) is titled "Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 Conjecture and Variations" and "published in the Journal of Number Theory, volume 222, 2021, pp. 1--20". Its conjecture is the system m = x^2+y^2+z^2+t^2, n^2 = x+3y+5z. Its bibliography cites the 1-3-5 literature in JNT and Acta Arith., none in ERA.
- The conjecture itself is stated in OEIS A303656 (%C: "Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for all n > 1. In other words, any integer n > 1 can be written as the sum of two squares, a power of 3 and a power of 5") and in arXiv:1701.05868v10, Conjecture 4.1(i) (the $3500 prize is in Remark 4.1).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this bullet, or replace it with the published version of the arXiv source: Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of four squares", Int. J. Number Theory 15 (2019), no. 9, 1863-1893 (Conjecture 4.1(i)). To keep the 1-3-5 paper as related work, cite it correctly (A. Machiavelo, N. Tsopanidis, J. Number Theory 222 (2021) 1-20, https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02592) and say that it proves a different conjecture of Sun.

reformulations.difference: OEIS defines a(n) as the number of representations n = a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d with a <= b, and conjectures a(n) > 0 for all n > 1. arXiv:1701.05868 Conjecture 4.1(i) states it as the set equality {a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d : a,b,c,d in N} = {2,3,4,...}. The Lean predicate `A` drops the ordering a <= b. The theorem asserts only `∀ n, 1 < n → A n`, i.e. the ⊇ half of the set equality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
Swapping a and b turns any representation into one with a <= b, so `A n` holds iff a(n) > 0. The ⊆ half of the set equality holds automatically: 3^c >= 1 and 5^d >= 1, so every such sum is at least 2. Both facts are proved in /workspace/review/final.lean using only standard axioms:
- `A n ↔ ∃ a b c d, a ≤ b ∧ n = a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d`
- `(∀ n, 1 < n → A n) ↔ {m | ∃ a b c d, m = a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d} = Set.Ici 2`

Also proved: ¬A 0 and ¬A 1, so the hypothesis 1 < n is exactly the source's domain. N in the source is {0,1,2,...}, so c = 0 and d = 0 (the power 1) are allowed, as in the Lean.

review.notes:
The mathematics in the file is faithful. `A n` is exactly "n = a^2+b^2+3^c+5^d with a,b,c,d in N = {0,1,2,...}". `conjecture` is "∀ n > 1, A n", which matches OEIS A303656's %C line and arXiv:1701.05868v10 Conjecture 4.1(i).

Checks on the Lean:
- The six test lemmas (A 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 25) are correct. The a_25 witness (1,4,1,1) is the OEIS example.
- A computable version of OEIS's count (with a <= b) matches the b-file exactly for n = 1..3000, and is positive for every n in 2..3000.
- The b-file is positive for every n in 2..100000.

Status: `research open` is current. OEIS revision #44 (May 30 2026) still says \"Conjecture\"; its latest note records a check up to 2.4*10^11 (Jul 2022). Sun's homepage still offers the $3500 prize and gives the same bound.

Smaller reference slips, not reported as findings:
- The bullet 'Z.-W. Sun, \"Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem,\" Journal of Number Theory' links to Sun's talk slides of that title (Dec 2016), not the JNT article (J. Number Theory 175 (2017) 167-190, doi:10.1016/j.jnt.2016.11.008). Sibling files OEIS/281976 and OEIS/303639 cite the article by DOI.
- Both slide decks (Dec 2016 and Dec 2017) predate the conjecture (A303656 was created Apr 27 2018) and do not contain it. They are background only.

The OEIS side remark (two squares + a power of 2 + a power of 3) and the arXiv paper's other parts of Conjecture 4.1 are not formalised. Leaving them out is not a defect.
